mutations.name: the-regex-narrows-back-to-pass-indices-only
mutations._mechanism: The original defect. A surface-suffixed audit is inside the `*.audit.v*.md` glob but rejected by the regex, so the module reports fewer cycles than were run and a caller reads the shortfall as 'no audits'. Nothing raises.

mutations.name: the-regex-admits-any-tail
mutations._mechanism: The mirror direction, and the reason a widening is not automatically an improvement. `.v26.codex.draft.md` is a draft, not an audit report; admitting it hands `_audit_issue` a file with no gate headings at exactly the moment the operator is told the gate passed. A test that only checks the too-narrow direction scores this mutant as survived.

mutations.name: the-cycle-representative-is-picked-from-the-other-end
mutations._mechanism: Determinism is the whole claim of the sort, and any single pick looks equally correct on a tree with one file per cycle. Only a cycle holding two surfaces can tell the ends apart -- which is why the pin builds one.
mutations.find: return {version: paths[0] for version, paths in groups.items()}
mutations.replace: return {version: paths[-1] for version, paths in groups.items()}

mutations.name: an-archived-copy-counts-as-a-second-audit
mutations._mechanism: Archiving copies rather than moves, so nearly every archived cycle exists twice under one filename. Counted as two, a one-auditor cycle reports every finding twice and reads like a two-auditor cycle -- inflation that looks like extra rigour.

mutations.name: the-collapse-folds-two-surfaces-into-one
mutations._mechanism: The opposite error in the same line: key on something coarser than the filename and `.codex` and `.agy` at one cycle become a single audit. The gate then reads one auditor while reporting that it read the cycle.

mutations.name: the-gate-scores-only-the-first-audit-of-the-cycle
mutations._mechanism: The false PASS this feature exists to close. Two auditors ran the same cycle and disagreed; scoring the first alone clears the gate and names a real, clean file as the evidence. Indistinguishable from a genuinely clean cycle in every output the operator sees.

mutations.name: the-dashed-phase-spelling-goes-back-to-empty
mutations._mechanism: `impl-plan` is how every other h-mad surface spells the phase. Answering `{}` for it is not an error but a number -- zero audits -- and zero is a believable answer for a feature that has not been audited yet.

mutations.name: an-unknown-phase-falls-through-to-plan
mutations._mechanism: The alias must widen the accepted spellings without making the lookup total. A typo'd phase would otherwise return the plan phase's audits and gate the wrong document -- a wrong answer, where the old code at least gave an empty one.
